Ardent

AR-dent -- two syllables, stress on the first syllable, AR. · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Ardent is enthusiastic or passionate.

An ardent guardian of the night sky, Mr. Vega petitions the county every year to dim its streetlights.

Worked Example

The lighthouse preservation society has exactly nine members, and Edna has been one of them for forty-one years -- painting rails, writing newsletters, and defending the old tower at every town meeting.

Edna is ardent: passionately devoted to her cause through decades of loyalty. Ardent burns like fervent, but its heat takes the shape of devotion -- attachment to a team, a cause, or a person that keeps showing up year after year.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

devoted: loyal and committed to someone or something

zealous: filled with energetic, driven commitment

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

halfhearted: done with little effort or interest

indifferent: having no interest or concern

Where it sits · how visibly the passion burns — devoted → ardent → zealous

devoted vs. ardent: Devoted is the steady, weaker base -- a devoted friend simply stays -- while ardent devotion burns visibly: it recruits, defends, celebrates, and never whispers.

zealous vs. ardent: Zealous is the strongest of the three and can even overshoot: an ardent fan cheers through every losing season, but a zealous one may start pounding on the referee's car.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — ard-

root — ard-: to burn (Latin ardere)

suffix — -ent

suffix — -ent: being in a state of (Latin -entem)

Put it together

Put it together: Ardent comes from Latin ardere, 'to burn' -- ardent feeling is feeling on fire. English aimed that fire at loyalty: ardent supporters, ardent admirers, ardent defenders, all burning steadily for the thing they love.

Use the root in a new word: arson

Use the root in a new word: arson: The fire marshal ruled the warehouse blaze an act of arson.

Root Check

Word Choice

Ardent nearly always aims at something: an ardent supporter, an ardent admirer, an ardent defender of a cause. That aim separates it from its two closest neighbors -- fervent names the heat of a feeling itself, and avid names a healthy appetite for an activity. The ardent fan loves the team; the avid golfer loves the game.
